acc-euclid.title: Euclid, Elements, Book VII, Proposition 2: Greatest Common Measure
acc-euclid.notes: Clay Mathematics Institute translation and Greek; subtraction-style ancient construction; modern remainder loop is not quoted verbatim.

acc-mit-intro.title: Erik Demaine, Jason Ku, Justin Solomon, MIT 6.006 Spring 2020, Lecture 1: Introduction
acc-mit-intro.notes: Explicit problem as input-output relation, algorithm, correctness by induction, efficiency, asymptotic cost models.

acc-mit-notes.title: MIT 6.006 Introduction to Algorithms, Spring 2020, lecture notes index

acc-mit-complexity.title: Erik Demaine, MIT 6.006, Lecture 19: Complexity
acc-mit-complexity.notes: P, NP, reductions, complexity categories; lecture summary and educational resource.

acc-turing.title: Alan M. Turing, On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem (written 1936, published 1937)
acc-turing.notes: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society s2-42, 230-265; original paper provenance and date; full reasoning on SEP.

acc-sep-ct.title: The Church–Turing Thesis, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (2023 revision)
acc-sep-ct.notes: Sections 1 and 4-6 distinguish formal equivalence from informal thesis and distinguish physical/complexity variants.

acc-sep-comp.title: Computability and Complexity, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (2021 revision)
acc-sep-comp.notes: Sections 1 and 2 describe historical calculi, universality, halting undecidability, complexity.

acc-stanford-alg.title: Stanford CS161 Design and Analysis of Algorithms, lecture resources
acc-stanford-alg.notes: Lecture 2: Asymptotics, Worst-Case Analysis, MergeSort; lecture 3: recurrences.

acc-jhu-lower.title: Michael Dinitz and Jessica Sorrell, JHU 601.433/633 Lecture 6 (2025), Sorting Lower Bound and Linear-Time Sorting
acc-jhu-lower.notes: Theorem 6.2.1 p.1 and proof pp. 1-3: worst-case comparisons Ω(log(n!)); distinction from integer-key sorts.

acc-floyd.title: Robert W. Floyd, Assigning Meanings to Programs (1967)
acc-floyd.notes: Proceedings of Symposia in Applied Mathematics 19, pp. 19-32. Attribution of control-flow assertions and termination arguments; bibliographic record rather than claim of reading publisher full text.

acc-hoare.title: C. A. R. Hoare, An Axiomatic Basis for Computer Programming (1969)
acc-hoare.notes: Communications of the ACM 12(10), 576-580, 583. Formal rules for proving program properties; primary abstract accessible.

acc-bloch.title: Joshua Bloch, Extra, Extra — Read All About It: Nearly All Binary Searches and Mergesorts Are Broken (2006)
acc-bloch.notes: First-person account of integer overflow in binary search in Bentley and JDK; describes input size required to trigger.

acc-lean.title: Jeremy Avigad, Leonardo de Moura, Soonho Kong, Sebastian Ullrich, Theorem Proving in Lean 4, Chapter 8
acc-lean.notes: Recursion, induction, well-founded recursion; not evidence that this pack includes a checked Lean theorem.

acc-sep-tm.title: Liesbeth De Mol, Turing Machines, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (substantive revision 21 May 2025)
acc-sep-tm.notes: Sections 2.3 and 2.4.1–2.4.3: universality, diagonal and Turing original circle-free versus contemporary halting formulation; 2025 revision verified.

acc-mit-6045.title: MIT OpenCourseWare 6.045J / 18.400J, Automata, Computability, and Complexity, Spring 2011, lecture notes index
acc-mit-6045.notes: Index confirms lectures 6 (Turing machines), 7 (decidability), 8 (undecidability), and 9 (mapping reducibility and Rice theorem). Slides credited to Prof. Nancy Lynch; index rather than linked PDFs read.

acc-stanford-cs103.title: Stanford CS103 Reference (course archive), recognizable, decidable, and co-recognizable languages
acc-stanford-cs103.notes: Course reference indexes recognizer, decider, complement, and co-recognizable terminology; tool-visible search excerpts, not independent proof of the theorem.

acc-post1944.title: Emil L. Post, Recursively Enumerable Sets of Positive Integers and Their Decision Problems (1944)
acc-post1944.notes: Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society 50(5), 284–316; verified title, year and DOI; not claiming direct inspection of its technical proofs.

acc-rice1953.title: H. Gordon Rice, Classes of Recursively Enumerable Sets and Their Decision Problems (1953)
acc-rice1953.notes: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 74(2), 358–366; bibliography/DOI corroborated; source of named theorem, not falsely presented as fully read.

acc-kleene1956.title: Stephen C. Kleene (1956), Representation of Events in Nerve Nets and Finite Automata, in Automata Studies, pp. 3–41
acc-kleene1956.notes: Source accessible through university mirror; historical regular-events result, not a claim of full original-paper audit.

acc-rabin-scott1959.title: Michael O. Rabin and Dana Scott (1959), Finite Automata and Their Decision Problems, IBM J. Research and Development 3(2):114–125
acc-rabin-scott1959.notes: Publisher abstract verifies paper and scope, not line-by-line original proof.

acc-nerode1958.title: Anil Nerode (1958), Linear Automaton Transformations, Proceedings AMS 9(4):541–544
acc-nerode1958.notes: Named theorem attribution together with Myhill; article studies a different automata setting. Do not assume its text states modern right-congruence proof verbatim.

acc-stanford-history.title: Stanford University CS103 historical timeline of results
acc-stanford-history.notes: Background on Myhill, Nerode, Rabin/Scott chronology; course-authored historical summary, not a primary original theorem.

acc-mit2020.title: Michael Sipser, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.404J Theory of Computation (Fall 2020), lecture notes index, lectures 1–5, 7

acc-chomsky1956.title: Noam Chomsky (1956), Three Models for the Description of Language, IRE Transactions on Information Theory 2(3):113–124
acc-chomsky1956.notes: Publisher abstract verifies historical inquiry and phrasing; no claim of original full text audit.

acc-chomsky1959.title: Noam Chomsky (1959), On Certain Formal Properties of Grammars, Information and Control 2(2):137–167
acc-chomsky1959.notes: Publisher abstract discusses proper inclusions of generative classes; no claim of reproducing formal paper proof.

acc-barhillel1961.title: Yehoshua Bar-Hillel, Micha Perles, and Eli Shamir (1961), On Formal Properties of Simple Phrase Structure Grammars, 14:143–172

acc-earley1970.notes: Published cubic worst-case and other bounds as stated in abstract, not to be conflated with CYK.
